How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, March 19, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. IRISH AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of March 5, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – FEBRUARY 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for February 2024.

  D. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR
  THE 2023 CALENDAR YEAR

  Under the provisions of Government Code Section 65400(b), the Planning
  Division is required to provide an annual report to the California Department
  of Housing and Community Development (HCD) and to the Governor’s Office
  of Planning and Research (OPR) regarding the implementation of the General
  Plan’s Housing Element and how the City is meeting the regional housing needs
  for the community. The General Plan Annual Progress Report (APR) is an
  important tool to facilitate the implementation of the Housing Element and to
  assist in tracking and monitoring the City’s progress in addressing the regional
  housing needs allocation (RHNA), including the number of housing units
  permitted by income level, the status of the programs in the Housing Element,
  and efforts to remove governmental constraints. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in this staff report and direct staff to submit the housing report to
  the State Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

  E. 2023 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2023 – DECEMBER 2023

  Under provisions of Government Code Section 65400(a)(2), the City is required
  to provide an annual report each April to the City Council and the State
  Governor’s Office of Planning and Research (OPR) regarding the status of the
  General Plan and its implementation progress. The Planning Commission
  reviewed the information at their March 11, 2024 meeting, affirmed the
  information in the report and recommended it be forwarded to the City Council.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in this staff report and direct staff to submit the report to the Office
  of Planning and Research and State Department of Housing and Community
  Development.

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT’S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 7072(a) – SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 703 would renew and update Lexipol Policy 707,
  approve the annual Military Equipment List as required by Government Code
  Section 7072(a) and establish a new adoption process for any future changes
  to the military equipment list. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  703 entitled “Renewing and Approving the San Gabriel Police Department’s

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  4
   Updated Military Equipment Use Policy 707 and Finding that the Annual
  Military Equipment Report is in Compliance with Government Code Section
  7072(a), Approving the AB 481 Annual Report and the Updated Policy 707."

  G. FIRE APPARATUS PURCHASE IN THE AMOUNT OF $960,343.25
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-06]

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is seeking approval to purchase a Pierce
  Enforcer Triple Combination Fire Apparatus, as the replacement for a 2015
  apparatus. This purchase, slightly ahead of the normal replacement cycle, is
  being made on a 46-month delivery time and to avoid price increases due in
  the summer of 2024. The total purchase price of a Pierce Enforcer Triple
  Combination Apparatus excluding taxes, fees and performance bond is
  $992,429.94. A cash pre-payment discount of $123,563 reduces the total
  amount to $868,866.94. Total acquisition cost of the apparatus, when adding
  10.25% sales tax, performance bond and California Tire Fees is $960,343.25. A
  lease purchase option was offered for a three-year or five-year financing period.
  Since funds have been set aside in the City’s Fleet Maintenance Fund to replace
  Fire Department vehicles, staff are proposing to pay the full amount of the
  apparatus at the time of signing the purchase agreement, aiming to minimize
  interest costs. By paying the costs of the apparatus up front, the City is saving
  interest of up to $172,444.00 based on a rate of 5.77%, effective March 4, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a purchase agreement subject to final approval as to form by the City
  Attorney, in the amount of $960,343.25 for a Pierce Enforcer Triple Combination
  Rescue Apparatus and to adopt Resolution No. 24-06.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. BUSINESS LICENSE TAX MODERNIZATION

  On February 6, 2024, the City Council received the results of the business license
  tax study along with recommended changes to the code that will modernize
  the City’s business license tax code and generate a moderate amount of
  additional tax revenue. Alternative recommended changes to the business

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  5
   license tax code were also provided. Following discussion, the City Council
  requested that the item be brought back at a future meeting. This item
  reintroduces the modernization of the business license tax code for further
  discussion and direction from the City Council. Staff’s recommendation to the
  business license tax code will generate an estimated additional revenue of
  $67,000. Staff’s alternative recommendation, adding a 20% increase to the flat
  rates, will generate an estimated additional $202,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  To modernize the tax structure, increase fairness, and generate additional
  revenue, staff recommends the City Council direct staff to bring back a
  resolution to place a measure on the November ballot that will ask voter to
  approve the following changes to the business license tax code:
  •  Add commercial rental category – assessed at $.75 per $1,000 in gross
  receipts.
  •  Remove the $1,050 not-to-exceed provision in the tax code.
  •  Add a provision to annually increase the flat rate taxes by the October
  consumer price index.
  •  Modify the coin-operated machines; vending machines category to vending
  machines and change the tax structure from 6% of the gross receipts to
  $1.50 per thousand in gross receipts.
  •  Add a catch-all miscellaneous category – assessed at $.50 per $1,000 in
  gross receipts.

  Alternative Recommendation

  As an alternative recommendation, staff recommends, in addition to the
  changes above, the additional changes:

  •  Add an increase to the business license tax for the flat rate taxes of 20% of
  the current flat rate amount.
  •  Remove the $450 cap for the residential rental classification.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 MID-YEAR BUDGET UPDATE [RESOLUTION NO.
  24-12]

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  6
   The mid-year budget update report examines the financial results of the general
  fund and Mission Playhouse fund through January 31, 2024. The mid-year
  financial information is analyzed, budget projections for both revenues and
  expenditures are updated, and mid-year budget adjustments are proposed. The
  results of the review are presented to the City Council. As outlined in Resolution
  No. 24-13, the mid-year adjustments proposed by departments will result in a
  net increase in general fund appropriations of $3,000. This stems from mid-year
  departmental budget requests of $944,000, which are off-set by vacancy savings
  of $941,000. Furthermore, other City funds have requested appropriation
  increases, $19,000 for Mission Playhouse fund, $10,000 for Proposition C local
  return fund, and $90,000 for development impact fee fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the mid-year budget
  update report and adopt Resolution No. 24-13 approving mid-year adjustments
  to Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget and Resolution No. 24-12 approving mid-year
  departmental staffing adjustments.

  B. AGREEMENT WITH CHINATOWN SERVICE CENTER FOR CASE
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $53,328.08 ANNUALLY,
  AND APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-10 AMENDING FISCAL YEAR
  2023-2024 BUDGET TO INCREASE APPROPRIATIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $18,750

  Staff have received requests from City Council, the Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission and community members, to develop a program
  or service which addresses the essential needs of residents requiring mental
  health or general assistance and resources. Staff have researched what services
  are provided by other cities to address this need and have provided potential
  partnership opportunities that may best serve the residents of San Gabriel. The
  HEAR Commission reviewed an initial proposal at the January 23, 2024 regular
  meeting and recommended that the program be moved forward to the City
  Council for approval. Should the City Council approve the addition of the
  contracted service, funds would need to be allocated from the General Fund to
  the Community Services Contractual Services account, 121-850-10-22-000 in
  the amount of $18,750 for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. The annual cost for the service
  through Chinatown Service Center is $53,328.08 and $93,750 through YWCA San

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 19, 2024  7
   Gabriel Valley. Depending on which vendor the City Council approves, staff will
  include the cost in the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget for approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the partnership with Chinatown
  Service Center to provide case management services to the public, adopt
  Resolution No. 24-10, authorizing the budget adjustment of $18,750 and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the professional services agreement with
  the selected provider.

  Alternatives to Staff Recommendations

  Should the City Council not wish to approve the staff recommendation, the
  following options are available:
  1. Send the item back to staff to research alternatives and bring the item back
  to City Council for review.
  2. Other options that the City Council determines after discussing the item.

  C. CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  The City Council will select a new Mayor and Vice-May for the coming year.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 2, 2024 at

MINUTES OF MARCH 19, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:30 P.M. on Tuesday, March 19, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wu .

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public
  Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edward Elizalde, Acting Fire Division Ch ief David
  Milligan, and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the agenda order was
  approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. IRISH AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH

  Mayor Harrington made the presentation and Sue Fitzsimmons, President of
  Partners with San Gabriel K9s, accepted the proclamation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  The following spoke or provided comments in favor of disbanding the Human Equity,
  Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission: George Carney, resident; Douglas Richter,
  resident; Cheryl Cabot, resident; and Carina Rivera, resident.
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING M INUTES  Page 1 of 6  March 19, 2024
   The following spoke or provided comments in favor of continuing the HEAR
  Commission: Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident; Jeanne Raya, resident; Christian Port;
  Evelyn Torres-Rangel, resident; Domingo Torres-Rangel, resident; Viki Goto, resident;
  Julian Loza, resident; Wai Tse; Sung Tse; Cathleen Chavez-Morris, resident; Robert
  Aizumi; Marsha Aizumi; Michelle Brenhaug, resident; Aaron Situ, resident; Kelly Munoz
  Rios, resident, HEAR Commission Youth Ambassador; Vicky Trieu, business owner; Alan
  K. Chan; Andrew, resident; Florence Simpson,· resident; Q. Sanchez, resident; Kathay
  Feng, resident; Violet Rose Wang; Gabriel Frank-McPheter, resident; Dr. Felix L. Nunez,

I  resident;  Isaac Chan, resident; Hilda Solis, Supervisor, First District, Board of
  Supervisors; Jorge Herrera-Avila, resident; Teresa Metcalf-Yzaguirre, resident; Andrew,
  resident; Geoff Kahan; and five anonymous commenters.

  The following spoke or provided comments expressing concerns related to the HEAR
  Commission and/or the proposed All Are Welcome program: Sue Fitzsimmons,
  resident, Partners with San Gabriel K9S; George Valdez, resident; D. Gutierrez, resident;
  and two anonymous commenters.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Council Member Chan noted a correction to Item 4C: on page 2 of the staff report,
  second paragraph, second to the last line, in the parentheses, should read February
  2023.

  In regard to Item 4G, in response to a question from Council Member Chan as to how
  much the engine to be retired would be sold for, City Manager Lazzaretto responded
  it would be sent to auction.

I  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4G as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of March 5, 2024.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved February 23, and March 1, 2024, Registers of Demands

I  and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - FEBRUARY 2024

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for February
  2024.

  D. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE
  2023 CALENDAR YEAR

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  March 19, 2024
   The City Council received and filed the Report and directed staff to submit the
  Housing Report to the State Department of Housing and Community Development
  (HCD).

  E. 2023 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2023 - DECEMBER 2023

  The City Council received and filed the Report and directed staff to submit the
  Report to the Office of Planning and Research and State Department of Housing

I  and Community Development.

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT'S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 7072(a) - SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 703 entitled: "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of San Gabriel, California, Readopting Police
  Department Lexipol Policy Section 707, Military Equipment, Pursuant to Assembly
  Bill (AB) 481 Military Equipment Acquisition, Use, and Reporting and Establishing
  Annual Review Process."

  G. FIRE APPARATUS PURCHASE IN THE AMOUNT OF $960,343.25 [RESOLUTION
  NO. 24-06]

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to enter into a purchase agreement,
  subject to final approval as to form by the City Attorney, in the amount of

I  $960,343.25 for a Pierce Enforcer Triple Combination Rescue Apparatus and
  adopted Resolution No. 24-06.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. BUSINESS LICENSE TAX MODERNIZATION

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included when the proposed tax rate change would take
  effect and notification of changes to business owners.

  Jorge Montes provided comments in opposition to a tax increase.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

I  The meeting was recessed at 8:35 P.M. and reconvened at 8:43 P.M. with all Council
  Members present.

  Discussion included that business license tax hasn't been updated for 30 years;
  concerns with using up political capital for not much gain and how it would affect
  the chances of a public safety building bond passing in the future; clarification on
  the staff recommendation; number of votes needed for the measure to pass;
  benefit of having lower business license taxes than neighboring cities; preference
  to have a higher cap instead of removing the cap; gross receipts may be
  understated due to self-reporting and are difficult to verify; how many properties
  would be affected by the rental cap; and a straw poll to determine if Council
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  March 19, 2024
   Members were interested in putting any business tax increase on the ballot at this
  time.

  A motion was made by Council Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu, to direct
  staff to return with a proposal, with the staff recommendation plus additional
  options for consideration, for a resolution placing a measure on the November
  2024 ballot.

  Motion failed by a vote of 2-3 as follows:

I  AYES:
  NOES:
  MENCHACA, WU,
  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 MID-YEAR BUDGET UPDATE [RESOLUTION NO. 24-
  12]

  Assistant Finance Director Linda Tang made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included methodology for the 5-Year General Fund
  projection; details of the capital lease line item; projected revenue from business
  license fees and permits; and transfers from the General Fund to the Mission
  Playhouse.

  Andrew, resident, commented on Other Post Employment Benefits (OPEB) and

I  CalPERS obligations, revenue from the sale of FEMA trailers, and funds budgeted
  for the prosecution of local misdemeanors.

  Mayor Harrington and City Manager Lazzaretto responded that these items will be
  discussed during the upcoming budget meetings and provided additional details.

  Discussion included evidence money details; current cash reserve of 25%;
  methodology for revenue projections on projects under development; new
  supervisor classifications in Public Works; desire to see transfers in to Mission
  Playhouse separated, progress made in Mission Playhouse revenues; details of
  projections for state sales tax and Measure SG sales tax; and kudos for the staff
  presentation.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to receive and file the mid-year budget update report and adopt Resolution
  No. 24-13 approving mid-year adjustments to Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget and
  Resolution No. 24-12 approving mid-year departmental staffing adjustments.

I
  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. AGREEMENT WITH CHINATOWN SERVICE CENTER FOR CASE MANAGEMENT
  SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $53,328.08 ANNUALLY, AND APPROVAL OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-10 AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET TO
  INCREASE APPROPRIATIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF $18,750

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  March 19, 2024
   Community Services Manager Matthew Morales-Stevens made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included case manager location, work hours, and employee
  management; the number of people served would depend on individual needs and
  would be assessed in a year; the agreement could be amended in the future to add
  additional services; 25 hours/week for the first year is a trial period to assess need;
  amending the agreement with an escalator to allow for more hours for increased
  needs; agreement details including flexibility; and public outreach to publicize the

I  new services.

  Andrew, resident; and Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez,  resident  and  HEAR
  Commissioner; commented in favor of the agreement.

  Discussion included that the primary focus is to have a case manager that can
  speak Mandarin/Cantonese as staff is available to help with Spanish translation;
  and that this provider is not focused on homelessness services, but rather
  preventative measures.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Ding, to:
